statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC s.147, s.148, s.452, s.506, s.323, s.302, s.326 (charged); convicted under IPC s.302, s.452 (Budhi Singh) and s.452, s.326, s.323 (Achhar Singh)

confession.reason: No confession or admission by the accused is mentioned.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Axe blow to the head of an elderly victim, with knowledge that it would in all probability cause death

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Accurately reflects the Court's reasoning on aggravating facts.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating facts are noted in the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.correct_value: All accused acquitted by Additional Sessions Judge, Mandi, giving benefit of doubt (24.02.1998)

trial_court_outcome.reason: Matches the trial court's acquittal and date.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: Acquittal of Budhi Singh and Achhar Singh set aside; Budhi Singh convicted under ss.302 and 452 IPC (life with fine); Achhar Singh convicted under ss.452, 326, 323 IPC (5 years RI with fine); acquittal of other five upheld
high_court_outcome.quote: Budhi Singh ... sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life along with fine ... Achhar Singh ... five years
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court actions and sentences are accurately reflected.

final_outcome.quote: Budhi Singh's conviction under Sections 302 and 452 IPC by the High Court are maintained
final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed appeals and maintained the convictions.

offence_finally_established.correct_value: Budhi Singh: IPC s.302 and s.452. Achhar Singh: IPC s.452, s.326 and s.323
offence_finally_established.quote: Achhar Singh's conviction under Sections 452, 326 and 323 IPC and Budhi Singh's conviction under Sections 302 and 452 IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: Matches the final conclusion of the Supreme Court.

imprisonment_type.quote: Budhi Singh has been convicted for offences under Sections 302 and 452 IPC and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life along with fine
imprisonment_type.reason: Life sentence for the principal accused (Budhi Singh) is supported; Achhar Singh's term is fixed.

imprisonment_years.reason: Null is acceptable as the main accused's sentence is life, not a fixed term.

fine_rs.quote: sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for five years along with fine
fine_rs.reason: Fines are mentioned without any rupee amount, so null is correct.

neutral_facts.reason: Neutral summary of incident and evidence; no names, outcomes or court references appear.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the statutory punishment range for s.302.

attempt_completion.quote: Swari Devi died due to a head injury
attempt_completion.reason: Death occurred, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.correct_value: Death of the elderly victim from a single fatal sharp-edged head injury (axe); injured male with incised wounds on face and posterior skull, facial bone fracture, and other grievous and simple injuries
physical_harm.quote: one fatal injury to the head by a sharp-edged weapon
physical_harm.reason: Injuries match the post-mortem and injury descriptions.

number_of_offences.reason: Seven charged sections and four distinct upheld sections are correctly counted.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Consistent eyewitness testimony (P.W.1, P.W.11, P.W.12) on fatal axe blow and axe attack; post-mortem report; doctor's testimony; axe recovery; house recoveries corroborated by P.W.14 and P.W.16
key_evidence_accepted.quote: independent witness P.W.14 also corroborated the recovery
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Accepted evidence matches the Court's relied-upon items.

witness_credibility.correct_value: Eyewitnesses exaggerated but core account consistent and matched medical evidence; no reason to falsely implicate; trial court erred in discarding evidence
witness_credibility.quote: The truth can be effortlessly extracted from their statements
witness_credibility.reason: Assessment of exaggeration, consistency and trial court error is accurately summarised.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: FIR not substantive evidence (Sheikh Hasib, Dharma Rama Bhagare); credibility not affected by relationship or exaggerations (Kishan Chand, Leela Ram); inconsistent evidence against one accused cannot benefit another (Gangadhar Behera, Prabhu Dayal)
prosecution_argument.quote: inconsistent evidence by the prosecution witnesses against one accused cannot be capitalised to give the benefit of doubt to another
prosecution_argument.reason: State counsel's arguments and cited authorities are accurately reported.

defence_argument.correct_value: Trial court's view was possible, so interference needed perversity (Murugesan, Aruvelu); exaggeration and false implication; single head injury in medical evidence; axe from public place; blood trail; police timing; no reason to attack on wedding day
defence_argument.quote: the four head injuries to the deceased as alleged by the eye-witnesses were falsified by the medical evidence

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Presumption of innocence doubled after acquittal; self-restraint and perversity test, but High Court may re-appreciate evidence fully; exaggeration separated from falsity; benefit of doubt only where firm conclusion not reached
legal_principle_applied.quote: there is no bar on the High Court's power to re-appreciate evidence in an appeal against acquittal
legal_principle_applied.reason: Principles applied by the Court are accurately captured.
